title: NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own): Cancellation Credit Computation and the Claim Bar
content:
### Cancellation credit — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)

**Date and reason.** The cancellation takes effect on the date and for the reason stated on the most recent signed cancellation request on the policy; the days of the current term run from the term start to the term end, and the term share is the days from the cancellation date to the term end divided by the days of the current term. A term that has already ended is fully earned, so only the current term's charges and credits are returned, except where the cancellation reaches back to the policy's inception.

**Standard credit.** The standard credit is the Pro Rata method applied to the current term as booked: the risk premium and reserve fund assessment booked at the term start, the term's endorsement charges and its re-rate credits each taken at the term share, the HFIAA surcharge and ICC premium taken at the term share, and the Federal Policy Fee and probation surcharge earned; no credit at all is returned when a claim bars the refund or the return is held.

**Risk premium and reserve fund credits.** Each of the risk premium and reserve fund credits combines the line's charge booked at the term start, its endorsement charges and its re-rate credits (the re-rate credits reducing it), each taken for the part of the term the rules give back; such a credit is never below zero and is rounded half-up to the cent (a half cent, within a tolerance of 0.0001 cent, goes to the higher cent). The HFIAA surcharge and ICC premium lines are each rounded half-up to the cent.

**Refund.** The refund paid out is the total of the cancellation credits, and it is paid to the payor of record.

**Claim bar.** A claim bars the refund when the reason is Replaced by Private Flood, Mortgage Paid Off, Voluntary — Not Required or Removed from SFHA by LOMA or LOMR and the claims file shows a claim with a date of loss in the current term that has been paid or is still open, read as follows.
- Each loss is placed by the whole calendar months counted back from the processing date to its date of loss: a loss fewer whole months back than the term start lies in the current term, and a loss the same number of whole months back as the term start lies in the boundary month, where only a loss whose date can be read is placed, by comparing that date with the term start.
- A payment bars the refund when the claims of the current term's whole months are paid net of voided payments above zero, or when the claims of the boundary month are paid net of voided payments above zero and the paid claim with the latest date of loss lies in the boundary month on or after the term start with its own payments net of voided payments above zero.
- An open claim bars the refund when the claim with the latest date of loss reported on the policy has a date of loss on or after the term start and has neither a payment nor a denial on record, as the base open-claim measure counts it.
- The claims file is clear of payments when the claims of the current term's whole months are not paid net above zero and either the boundary month's claims are not paid net above zero or the paid claim with the latest date of loss lies in the boundary month before the term start; it is clear of open claims when no claim is reported, when the claim with the latest date of loss reported on the policy has a date of loss before the term start, or when exactly one claim is reported in the current term's whole months and the boundary month together and it has a payment or a denial on record.

**Hold.** For a cancellation under one of the four claim-bar reasons whose claims file this reading finds neither barred nor clear, and only for such a cancellation, the current-term return is held: no cancellation credit and no refund are booked with the cancellation. For every other cancellation, no refund at all is due for the current term under the claim-bar reasons when a claim with a date of loss in the current term has been paid or is still open; the cancellation still proceeds.

**Hypothetical worked example** (invented figures; no claim; reason Building Sold). A 365-day term with 146 days left at the cancellation date, so the term share is 146 divided by 365. Risk premium booked at the term start 1,000.00 dollars, no endorsement charges or re-rate credits: risk credit 400.00. Reserve fund assessment 180.00: credit 72.00. HFIAA surcharge 250.00: credit 100.00. No ICC premium. Fees earned. Refund 572.00.
